_doc: One entry per deviation shape. Lifecycle and gating rules: docs/GATING.md. Never delete entries; never flip still_reproduces without a fresh verifying scan. `signal` is a `|`-joined list of canonical names — each token is either a bias-report metric (docs/bias_data.json `metrics`) or a registry signal key (LANGUAGE_DEFINITIONS rules, via tools/_registry.py); no prose, no `+`, no `(various)`; tokens are sorted and unique. The reports join `signal` x `languages_seen` as a cross-product to decide whether a cell is accounted for (docs/GATING.md n/a rule 2 today; red cells from gitgalaxy#2669 E.1), so a token must hold for EVERY language listed — scope a collective entry down rather than let it excuse a cell nobody looked at. An entry that explains no cell (a workflow or classification fact) carries an empty `signal`, which never matches. `languages_seen` may be the sentinel ["all"].

entries.verdict: galaxyscope.py ~2145 ('THE CONTEXTUAL BASELINE FIX'): a file imported by others (popularity > 0) has orphaned_logic converted into api before recording. Micro-repro: 2-def file imported by a sibling records api=4, un-imported records api=2. With the spec's main->a->b->c chain and uncalled probes, api = defs x 2 in a/b/c, defs in main. Deliberate scoring semantics; raw counts unrecoverable from the DB (filed squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2536 asking for raw recording). apex added 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.3): it had no import chain at all until Type.forName('a'/'b'/'c') was planted, so a/b/c had popularity 0 and api 0; with the chain live their 3 uncalled probes convert to api 3 each, exactly this shape. GATE KEY CHANGE (gitgalaxy#2729, 2026-09-04): the conversion no longer reaches the manifest's `api` -- verify_language.py reads raw_arch_api there -- and is pinned instead as `api_orphan_credit` = arch_api - raw_arch_api, which this entry now covers. Semantics unchanged: credit = the file's uncalled probe count in a/b/c (3), 0 in main (popularity 0). Still the gate's only assertion that the main->a->b->c import chain resolved.

Keywords inside one string literal ('if eval fails, try open') count toward branch (+2), safety (+1), io (+1) but eval does NOT count toward high_risk_execution (routes to sec_tainted_injection instead). Micro-repro: identical files differing only in literal content, scanned end-to-end. Comments are fully stripped (verified 0 contribution); strings are inconsistently half-counted. 2026-08-31 cross-language extension: javascript reproduces python exactly (same decoy sentence, if/try count, eval does not); cobol does NOT shield at all (ALTER counts high_risk_execution from inside a DISPLAY literal) — the shielding is lexical-family-dependent, i.e. itself a language bias. 2026-08-31 legacy batch: fortran/ada/assembly count literals like cobol (fortran IF+GOTO+OPEN all count; ada 'if' counts; asm jmp/syscall count, and ARM's single-letter 'b' mnemonic even matches the filename inside %include "b.asm"); abap is a THIRD profile — shields branch/high_risk/io but NOT safety (TRY in a literal counts safety, isolated by micro-repro with comment-only vs string-only files). Worst amplification: a branch keyword inside a literal creates phantom branch context that triples state_mutation via the flux weighting (see state-flux-branch-weighting). Current behavior baked into manifests; whether intentional is the upstream question. 2026-08-31 batch 3 (12 mainstream languages): the selective profile (high-risk family shielded, branch/safety/io count) holds for c/cpp/csharp/java/go/kotlin/typescript/php/lua/swift; ruby counts eval from the literal (eval-as-bypass, like shell); perl's eval survives only because its bypass rule requires eval-followed-by-quote/paren (syntax shielding, not surface shielding); swift's api rule counts the word 'open' inside the literal (API-exposure mass from prose). try counts branch in csharp/java/kotlin/php/perl/swift/typescript. Swift's bare-open api FP filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2544. 2026-08-31 batch 4 (Tier-1 completion): a FOURTH profile — scheme's sexp-anchored branch keywords shield strings by SYNTAX (bare 'if' in a literal cannot match the paren-anchored rule) while its unanchored eval still counts; m4 is fully inert by the same mechanism (macro-name keywords). matlab and tcl join shell/ruby in counting eval-as-bypass from literals. dockerfile/makefile/livecode count literals wholesale. swift-open-style api hit not repeated elsewhere. RESOLVED-AS-EXPLAINED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy#2535 closed as not-a-bug after root-cause isolation. There is NO string-literal shielding mechanism anywhere in the engine -- strings are never stripped/masked from the code stream for any structural signal, in any language (only comments are). Every observed 'shielding' shape here is the ordinary Silencer Region dampener (spatial_correlation.py apply_dampener_correlations Block 2: high_risk_execution <- safety, 500-char radius) firing because the shared decoy sentence 'if eval fails, try open' happens to contain both a real danger keyword AND a real safety keyword for SOME languages, by accident of English-word/rule-vocabulary overlap -- not a deliberate per-language shielding design. Isolated via direct micro-repro: python state_danger 0->1 the instant 'try' is swapped out of the decoy with nothing else changed. Per-language explanation for the profiles recorded above: python/js/haskell/abap ('shielded'/'inverted') all have TRY (or their language's equivalent) in their OWN safety rule, so the dampener fires; cobol/fortran/ada/assembly ('unshielded') do NOT have TRY in their safety rule (cobol's is END-IF/END-PERFORM/.../VALIDATE/CHECK), so it never fires; rust's 'shielded' reading was actually a THIRD, unrelated cause -- its high_risk_execution rule has no 'eval' concept at all (panic!/todo!/process::exit), a morphology mismatch, not shielding. The #2546 'phantom branch trigger from string literals' shares this exact explanation (no shielding exists, so a genuinely-present branch keyword correctly triggers the flux dampener regardless of surface). Follow-up filed as a CORPUS issue (decoy sentence design), not an engine issue -- see keyword-rosetta issue tracking decoy redesign. capstones jcl.md/cobol.md/python.md corrected to match. DECOY REDESIGN PILOT 2026-09-01 (keyword-rosetta#17): python/fortran/rust re-authored to a danger-only literal ('plain eval|ASSIGN|abort decoy text') per the redesigned SPEC §String decoy. All three profiles converge on the same clean read -- the danger keyword counts +1 from inside the literal, undampened: python eval +1 (was 0 under the old sentence's try-collision), fortran ASSIGN +1 (GOTO retired from the decoy: it doubles as a branch keyword and fed the x3 flux -- state_mutation 6->2), rust abort +1 (the first time rust's decoy tested anything; eval matches nothing in its danger rule; state 6->2). One new engine fact surfaced by the pilot and now recorded in SPEC: dampener correlations are function-scoped, but MODULE-LEVEL code falls back to flat 500-char-radius behavior (apply_dampener_correlations docstring) -- python's literal initially read 0 at module level because probe_safety's assert sat ~450 chars away; moving it inside probe_globals isolated it. DECOY REDESIGN COMPLETE 2026-09-02 (gitgalaxy#2669 A.1 wave 2, 32 languages; A.3 wave 3, abap/assembly/cobol/sqlite): all 40 languages_seen now carry a danger-only literal, gates green. Screening rule that made it mechanical: run the candidate literal through the language's live compiled rules and require exactly one high_risk_execution hit and zero hits in any SCORED column -- the planted set plus the seven non-planted signals that feed a risk_* formula (_registry.risk_dependencies(): concurrency, sync_locks, reflection_metaprogramming, immutability_locks, spec_exposure, debug_prints, llm_api). That rejected Thread.Abort (csharp), Thread.stop (java) and iex (powershell), each clean against the planted set alone. Filler words need the same check: 'text' matches dart's and embedded_python's ui_framework rule. Findings from the sweep: matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval under safety_bypasses, NOT high_risk_execution, so their old decoy exercised the wrong family (safety_bypasses 3->2 each); swift's api rule counted the prose 'open' (api 4->3, a scored planted column fed from inside a string, the #2544 shape); abap's recorded 'third profile' was the Silencer Region after all -- dropping TRY takes its TRUNCATE 0->1; scheme moved no count at all, its sexp-anchored branch rule never having matched the prose 'if'; assembly keeps its x3 flux because probe_state's own 'ret' is a branch keyword, unlike the 35 languages where the retired 'if' was the only branch in scope. sqlite needs a two-word literal ('DROP DATABASE') -- its danger vocabulary has no single bare token. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the field now names every column this shape moves, not just the headline four — state_mutation (the x3 flux amplification), safety_bypasses (matlab/ruby/shell/tcl match eval there, not under high_risk_execution) and api (swift's rule counting the prose 'open', #2544) are consequences recorded in the verdict above and are joined on here.

python's test rule includes \bassert\b and the safety rule includes assert: one planted assert counts both. Legitimate overlapping taxonomies; record +1 test wherever a safety assert is planted. Also c (bare assert( in both rules) and perl (ok( in the test rule alongside croak/confess safety plants). RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (assert removed from the test rule, still matched by safety): a.py test dropped 3->2. Still reproduces for c/perl (their own rule files are unchanged).

python-family io rule matches the os./sys. prefixes that the globals plants (os.environ, sys.argv) necessarily carry: +2 io in whichever file hosts probe_globals. RESOLVED for python via gitgalaxy #2626 (io rule gained negative lookaheads excluding os.environ/sys.argv from the io match): a.py io dropped 3->1. No other language currently in languages_seen.

Debt rules are whole-text, not comment-anchored, and '-' is a regex word boundary: HACK-LEVEL (data item, 2 code occurrences) counts fragile_debt, PROBE-TODO (paragraph name) counts planned_debt. Python's HACK_LEVEL is inert only because '_' is a word character — tokenization luck, not surface anchoring. Real-world FP shapes: COBOL BUG-COUNT/WS-FIX-FLAG, css .bug-icon, lisp fix-me. Filed upstream; observed counts baked into cobol manifest until fixed. Batch 4: scheme reproduces it — (define (probe-todo ...)) records planned_debt 2 (comment + identifier), confirming the lisp-family exposure predicted in #2537. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2622 (closes #2537) — hyphenated-identifier guards ((?<![A-Za-z0-9]-) / (?!-[A-Za-z0-9])) on the shared GLOBAL_FRAGILE_DEBT/GLOBAL_PLANNED_DEBT patterns. Fresh verifying scan (engine at PR #2622 head): cobol c.cpy fragile_debt 3->1, planned_debt 2->1; scheme c.scm planned_debt 2->1 — only the planted * HACK: / * TODO: / ;; TODO: comments count. Real comment markers incl. the hyphen-adjacent family (-- TODO, --TODO, TODO--) verified still counting via the upstream PR's strict tests. Manifests re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4.

A bare token + period in Area B (CEE3DMP. / CEEMOUT., column 12) is counted as a paragraph header: func_start regex's post-sequence-area [ \t]* tolerates any indentation (relaxed/free-format support). By strict reference format a paragraph-name must start in Area A. b.cpy records func_start 5 (3 real paragraphs + 2). Whether the relaxed tolerance is deliberate is the upstream question. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2552 (closes #2538 -- func_start no longer mistakes LE service calls for paragraphs). Fresh verifying scan (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2552/#2611): b.cpy func_start 5->3, api 5->3 (orphan conversion follows), telemetry/safety_bypasses/state_mutation unchanged at 2/2/2 -- only the two bare-token FPs vanished. Manifest re-baselined in the same change per GATING step 4. Surfaced by the first all-language CI run since #2552 merged (rosetta PR #5, which touches no data/ so the gate ran all 46).

'with (shape) {}' is parsed as a function named 'with' by the identifier(args){ alternation: the keyword exclusion list has if/for/while/switch/catch/return but not with. finditer-confirmed; switch (flag) {} in the same corpus is correctly excluded. b.js records func_start/args 4 for 3 functions. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2539 ('with' added to the func_start/args statement-keyword exclusions, JS and TS): b.js func_start/args/api 4->3.

cobol globals pattern includes WORKING-STORAGE\s+SECTION as an alternative — every fixed-format program with a working-storage section records globals >= 1. keyword_menu.py missed it (multi-word alternation; the miner only validates single-token candidates) — menu-tool improvement noted. main.cbl globals 1 baked in.

Token signals match ordinary identifiers that happen to spell a keyword: js probeIo's parameter named 'path' counts io +1 (path is a js io keyword). Inherent to keyword-based signals. Authoring guidance: avoid naming identifiers after menu keywords unless the collision is the point; record it when unavoidable. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): narrowed from the prose '(any token signal)' to `io`, the one collision actually verified (javascript probeIo's `path` parameter). The shape generalises but the ledger must not claim to explain a cell nobody has looked at; a new collision is a new occurrence, added when observed.

state_mutation is recorded x3 when branch context exists in the file ('flux' semantics, matching the state_flux column name). Micro-repro: one := inside a real ada if -> 3; one := with no branch -> 1; the multiplier applies file-wide to all mutations. python/cobol corpus files were exact only because their b files had no branch context. Consequence of #2535: a branch keyword inside a string literal creates PHANTOM branch context and triples unrelated real mutations ('while' in a string: 2 raw := -> 6). REFINED (batch 3, go micro-evidence): the x3 weighting is PER-FUNCTION, not per-file — go b.go records 11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 (its own string carries the branch keyword) + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1 (no branch context in that function). Reproduces in all 12 batch-3 languages whose state rules have raw hits alongside the string decoy. Batch 4 adds the three cleanest per-function proofs: matlab main = 12 = one function's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1; powershell c stays x1 because probe_debt has no return/branch while its sibling does; dockerfile scopes flux per RUN instruction (4 = 1x3 + 1x1). DOCUMENTED 2026-09-01: gitgalaxy PR #2631 (closes #2546) resolves the upstream question as deliberate design, kept and now documented + test-pinned. SEMANTICS CORRECTION to this entry's earlier description: the x3 is a 150-CHARACTER proximity radius per mutation within the same function (spatial_correlation.py Block 6, correlate_scoped) -- NOT a blanket per-function branch-context toggle; corpus probe functions were simply shorter than the radius, which masked the distinction (the per-function refinement was correct about scoping, wrong about the trigger being function-wide). Raw counts are recoverable as recorded - 2*amplified_cascading_flux (per-file mitigation_telemetry, audit report 'Contextual Mitigations & Amplifications'). Behavior unchanged, so still_reproduces stays true; the actionable blocker for the corpus's state_mutation median inflation is now #2535 ALONE (the phantom literal trigger) -- language tracking issues' state_mutation residuals re-point there. 2026-09-01 (gitgalaxy#2634 / #2545 landing): this entry's powershell `c` evidence line no longer discriminates — with `return` out of `branch`, probe_todo has no branch context either, so powershell c is x1 throughout and c branch is 0. The go / matlab / dockerfile per-function proofs are untouched and remain this entry's evidence. Same landing removes the phantom `return` context that was tripling apex c.cls (state_mutation 3 -> 1, re-baselined with it): a real reduction in flux inflation, not a semantics change. 2026-09-03 (gitgalaxy#2654 / engine PR gitgalaxy#2703): the matlab per-function proof is RETIRED and matlab drops out of languages_seen. matlab main.m's `12 = probe_branch's 3 raw x3 + three functions' 1 raw x1` only ever existed because every one of those raw hits was the `out = <value>` return convention counted as a mutation -- probe_branch's three `out = k` are three `return k`, which every other language records as zero. With the engine's `matlab_return_channel` scope filter the file records 0, and no matlab probe function now has a mutation alongside branch context, so the language exhibits no flux amplification at all. It was NOT re-planted: a matlab-only mutation added to keep the demonstration would break the 12-probe program's cross-language equivalence, which is what makes this corpus able to find shapes like #2654 in the first place. go's b.go (11 = probe_state's 3 raw x3 + probe_bypass's 2 raw x1) and dockerfile's per-RUN scoping (4 = 1x3 + 1x1) are unaffected and remain this entry's per-function evidence.

'USE A' does not resolve to a.f90 in the dependency DAG (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires); 'USE a' resolves. Fortran is case-insensitive, the suffix-map lookup is not. Corpus lowercased its USE targets to keep the DAG probe live; real uppercase legacy fortran (very common) silently loses its dependency graph. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2540 (per-language case-folded fallback in the DAG suffix-map lookup for fortran/cobol/haskell, scoped to the importing language's own files): uppercase 'USE A' now resolves; corpus values unchanged (targets were lowercased as the workaround). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api` — the two the verdict actually pins (popularity stays 0, orphan->api conversion never fires). The corpus never showed the wider graph family deviating because the USE targets were lowercased as the workaround.

ada's closing 'end if' re-matches \bif\b: every well-formed if statement counts branch at least twice (if + end if). Same class would apply to fortran 'END IF' spelled with a space (corpus used ENDIF, which is inert). Inherent to token-based branch counting on block-closed languages; baked in (main.adb branch 4).
GOTO is in both fortran's branch rule and its high_risk_execution rule — one planted GOTO counts both. finditer-confirmed.

assembly's branch rule includes call and ret (all control transfers) — correct for asm morphology but it means every probe body's ret and every glue call counts branch (main.asm: 10 = 3 call + 4 ret + 3 planted jumps). Cross-language branch comparisons must expect asm to run structurally hot.

ARM's single-letter 'b' branch mnemonic matches the word b anywhere literals count — including the filename inside %include "b.asm" (a.asm branch +1, finditer-confirmed). Any asm file mentioning a bare 'b' in a string/path gains branch mass. Sub-case of #2535's literal counting; not filed separately.

Top-level value bindings (CAFs like 'region = unsafePerformIO ...') count func_start/args like any function binding — morphologically correct for haskell, where top-level values ARE nullary functions. a.hs records 5 (3 probes + 2 planted globals). Type-signature + binding pairs count once, not twice (verified).
finally is in both haskell's cleanup and safety rules (finditer-confirmed on c.hs) — one planted finally counts both.

shell's branch rule counts the test brackets [ and ] as branch tokens (finditer on main.sh: if,[,],then,fi = 5 for one conditional) — every bracketed test costs +2 branch on top of if/then/fi. Defensible ([ is the test builtin) but a strong per-language inflation for cross-language branch comparisons.

'trap : TERM' counts globals: the TERM signal name collides with the TERM env-var keyword in shell's globals rule (a.sh globals 3 for 2 planted). Any trap handler naming TERM/USER-adjacent signals inherits this.

On languages without a same-file call graph the orphan census includes non-function shapes, so the orphan->api conversion count diverges from visible function counts: shell a/b convert 4 with 3 functions (the extra tracks the source line), sqlite converts 2/4/3 with 3 CREATE INDEX each and main.sql records orphaned_logic 7 for 4 indexes. Recorded as observed; gitgalaxy#2536 (raw hit_vector recording) would make these auditable. RESOLVED 2026-08-31: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy PR #2618 (closes #2547 -- synthetic slicer bucket names excluded from the orphan/duplicate census). Fresh verifying scans (engine at gitgalaxy main post-#2618): the inflating orphans were the synthetic buckets themselves -- __global_context__ in livecode/lua/matlab/ruby/shell a- AND b-files (api -1 each; lua a 9->8, b 10->9), and sqlite b.sql/c.sql whose 'functions' are ALL synthetic names (CREATE_Statement/SELECT_Statement/UPDATE_Statement/Declarative_Block), so every conversion there vanishes (a.sql 2->0, b.sql 4->0, c.sql 3->0). Real probe functions unaffected everywhere; 13 manifest cells re-baselined in this change per GATING step 4. lua/ruby added to languages_seen (same __global_context__ shape, confirmed). dockerfile/powershell manifests needed no change (their counts never included the bucket). First live catch of the #2557 rosetta-audit system (run locally against pull/2618/head pre-merge).
^.read counts BOTH import and io (finditer-confirmed) — every corpus chain link adds +1 io in sqlite. By design (a .read is file io), but a cross-language io comparison must expect it.

GalaxyScope's census enumerates git-tracked files only; an untracked folder scans as '0 files mapped' with no per-file warning. Authoring workflow requires commit-before-verify (SPEC.md). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `signal` is deliberately EMPTY. This is a workflow fact, not an explanation for any cell — an untracked folder produces no numbers at all — and an empty signal never matches the metric x language join, so it can never excuse a deviation.

The <?php open tag's ? matches php's branch rule bare ternary-? alternation (finditer-confirmed): EVERY php file records branch >= 1 from its own open tag. A systematic per-file +1 on all real-world PHP; worth an upstream look at excluding ?> / <? tag context from the ? alternation. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2541 (tag context excluded from the ternary-? alternation via (?<!<)?(?!>) guards): per-file tag +1 gone, corpus php branch main 4->3, a/c 1->0, b 3->2.

kotlin's branch rule counts return: every file's branch = returns + real branch keywords (main.kt 8 = 5 returns + if/else/when; files with only returns record branch 3). Same cross-language-inflation class as assembly's call/ret. Batch 4: apex, objective-c, powershell, and zig (pattern-confirmed) also count return — it is a 5-language family, not a kotlin quirk; scala/dart/groovy siblings do not. Strengthens #2545's inconsistency framing. Batch 5: solidity is the 6th member (main branch 8 = 5 returns + 3 keywords). RESOLVED 2026-09-01: fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2545 (PR #2634). Checked 11 close siblings across every relevant family (java/c/rust/go/csharp/scala/dart/groovy/swift/typescript/cpp) -- none count bare return as branch, including rust/csharp which share kotlin/zig's exact early-return idiom; no defensible rationale found for any of the 6. Fix split by whether return was already tracked elsewhere: kotlin/apex/powershell/zig had it duplicated under structural_boundaries already (pure de-dup); objective-c/solidity had no other rule tracking it, so return moved there instead of being deleted (signal preserved, same convention). Re-verified against engine pull/2634/head: all 6 gates PASS, branch now matches planted intent EXACTLY in every file (main 3, b 2, a/c 0) across all 6 languages. Real downstream ripple confirmed and re-baselined: apex c.cls state_mutation 3->1 (the manifest's own pre-fix note had already predicted this -- c's return was providing phantom branch context that #2546's x3 flux weighting amplified; removing return-as-branch removed the phantom trigger, leaving the raw hit).

kotlin's object declaration is the globals plant AND counts class_start (a.kt class_start 2) — a documented tier-1 exception to the no-classes tripwire, like cobol's PROGRAM-ID: object IS kotlin's singleton-class construct.

swift's _dependency_capture requires module names of 2+ characters ([a-zA-Z_][\w.]+), so 'import a' captures nothing: the corpus's swift chain never resolves, popularity stays 0, and no orphan->api conversion fires. Real single-letter modules are rare but the +-quantifier looks unintentional next to other languages' * shapes. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2543 (capture tail [\w.]+ -> [\w.]*): 'import a' captures, the swift chain resolves, orphan->api conversion fires (a/c api 0->3, b 1->4). SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): scoped to `popularity|api`, the two the verdict pins.

go's safety_bypasses rule's dot-import alternation (\bimport\s+(?:\.[ \t]+)?") matches EVERY quoted import, not just dot-imports: +1 bypasses per importing file corpus-wide. The (?:\.[ \t]+)? being optional makes the dot-import detector fire on all imports. RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2542 (dot made mandatory in the alternation): plain quoted imports no longer count, corpus go safety_bypasses main/a 1->0, b 3->2.

Languages whose visibility IS a naming/declaration convention count it wholesale: go's encapsulation rule counts every lowercase top-level symbol (7-9 per corpus file), perl's counts every my declaration (3-4 per file). Correct morphology, but cross-language encapsulation comparisons must expect these to run structurally hot.

typescript's args rule counts statement-position call parens (describe(kit), expect(kit)) in addition to declaration params — a.ts args 5 for 3 declarations (finditer-confirmed). Plants that are bare calls contaminate args in ts. Batch 4: apex and groovy count statement-position calls the same way (main args 7 = 4 sigs + 3 dispatch calls); objective-c over-counts via selector-colon segments (related morphology, recorded per-manifest).

m4 and scheme have _dependency_capture = None: include()/(import ...) count the import signal but can never produce a DAG edge, so popularity stays 0 and orphans never convert, corpus-wide. Two whole languages invisible to network_risk_sensor by construction — worth an upstream note whether deliberate. Batch 5: yacc (#include counted, capture None) and markdown (no import rule at all) join — four registry languages structurally invisible to the DAG. scheme RESOLVED via gitgalaxy#2652 (added _dependency_capture handling both the corpus's bare (import a) form and real R7RS/Guile library-list forms) -- removed from languages_seen; m4/markdown/yacc remain. SCOPE CORRECTION (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): markdown REMOVED from languages_seen — the entry had it as "no import rule at all", but a None `import` rule is not a None `_dependency_capture`. markdown defines a live capture (the inline-link form `[text](target)`) and its DAG resolves: dependency_links 3, popularity 0.75, betweenness 0.0833, producer_ratio 0.5, i.e. the same values as python/fortran/swift. Its `import` cell is n/a (no rule), which is markdown-lit-plane-morphology's business, not this entry's. m4 and yacc remain, and the scan confirms the full pinned profile they share: dependency_links 0, dependency_density 0, popularity 0, betweenness 0, closeness 0, producer_ratio 0, pagerank at the uniform 1/N 0.2, normalized_blast_radius 200, api 0 (orphans never convert) and therefore risk_api_exposure 0.0 against a 5.29 median — that last one is the red cell this entry has to own, so the signal list names it. Batch C's C.3 removes m4/yacc once #2652's capture shape is extended to them. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2685, Batch C.2 of gitgalaxy#2669, 2026-09-02): m4 and yacc both gained a _dependency_capture built on #2652's shape -- m4 for all four include spellings past m4 quoting, yacc for the prologue #include its `import` signal already counted -- so languages_seen is now empty and still_reproduces is false. Verified by a fresh scan on the engine PR, not by hand: the pinned profile this entry described is gone for both languages, replaced by exactly the healthy sibling profile (popularity 1/1/1/0, producer_ratio 0.5/0.5/1.0/0, non-uniform pagerank, dependency_density 1.0 on a/b and 0.1667-0.2 on main), and the red cell the entry owned -- risk_api_exposure 0.0 against a 5.29 median -- closes because api now converts (0 -> 3 on a/b/c, reblessed in this PR's manifests). The remaining orphan of this shape is neither m4 nor yacc: see gitgalaxy#2684, where the popularity tally credits every same-stemmed file in a scan, which is a different defect in the same subsystem.

Classification is per-file with no folder-context bleed: a .py file without its own micropython marker (import machine etc.) classifies as plain python even when every sibling is embedded — verified via the DB language column, twice (machine.idle() alone was NOT a sufficient discriminator; import machine was). Also two rule-level divergences on byte-similar code: embedded io drops os./sys. (python counts them), and orphan->api conversion does not fire under embedded classification. UPDATE 2026-08-31: the no-conversion divergence was fixed upstream by gitgalaxy#2548 (embedded_python never wired into Python-family indentation scoping — found independently by a tri-comparison sweep); orphan->api conversion now fires under embedded classification (api 6, verified by the CI gate's fresh scan against gitgalaxy main). The per-file classification and io-rule divergences still stand. First ledger entry re-baselined by an upstream fix — the GATING self-improvement loop closing end to end. SIGNAL SCOPE (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): `io|api` — the two measurable divergences (embedded's io rule drops the os./sys. prefixes python counts; orphan->api conversion, since fixed by gitgalaxy#2548). The per-file classification itself is not a metric and is not joined on.

dart's and zig's globals rules match final/const/var initializations at ANY indentation — function-local declarations count as globals (dart b/c +1 each from local finals; zig b 2 from function-local vars). AGC's real 1960s YUL/GAP instruction set (agc_assembly.py:99-101, comment: 'AGC lacks native objects') has no struct/record-defining pseudo-op -- its data/memory constructs (ERASABLE/FIXED MEMORY, EQUALS, 2DEC/2OCT, CADR/ECADR) are already fully covered by globals/memory_alloc/pointers. GNU M4 is a pure text-substitution macro processor; neither M4 nor Autoconf (the corpus's real-world use case) has any record/object/type-declaration concept. func_start already covers macro definition (m4_define/AC_DEFUN); reviewing the full rules dict (m4.py) finds no other m4/autoconf idiom resembling a compound-type or entity boundary. Unlike yacc or fortran, there is no sibling 'macro processor with a type system' in the registry to suggest this is an engine gap rather than the language's actual shape.

GNU Make's model is variables plus file/phony targets; it has no entity or type-declaration concept. The one candidate construct, `define ... endef` (a named multi-line template), is already correctly wired to `macros` (makefile.py:216) rather than an object/entity boundary -- it defines a reusable text template, not a typed record, and double-wiring it to class_start would misrepresent it as an OOP-like boundary it isn't. No record/struct idiom exists anywhere in real Makefile usage.

Comment at shell.py:119-121: 'Shell is strictly procedural.' The one candidate construct, associative arrays (`declare -A`), is a data-structure instance, not a type/entity declaration, and isn't wired anywhere (pointers/immutability_locks/encapsulation cover declare -n/-r but not -A). Unlike tcl, which has real, idiomatic OOP frameworks (TclOO/Snit/Itcl, wired at tcl.py:70-72) precisely because tcl programmers commonly use them, there is no comparably common bash-native class convention in real-world scripts to anchor a rule to.

CSS is purely declarative with no embedded imperative/scripting payload, unlike the other languages that wire these three signals only against such payload: html's cleanup/telemetry fire on inline JS (removeEventListener/clearInterval, <script src=analytics>/sendBeacon); dockerfile's fire on shell build steps (apt-get clean, LOG_LEVEL); yaml's telemetry fires on GH Actions workflow commands (::debug/::warning/::error). CSS never carries any of that. cleanup: no destructor/teardown lifecycle exists -- rules are declaratively re-evaluated per paint; the closest analog (unset/initial/revert/revert-layer) is already claimed by panics_and_aborts, so a cleanup rule over the same tokens would double-count; clear:both is a layout primitive, not resource teardown. state_mutation: custom-property declarations and cascade overrides are declaration/specificity resolution, not temporal reassignment (no 'was A, now B' model) -- mirrors html's identical state_mutation=None/identical stated reasoning; css and html are the two purely-declarative languages in the taxonomy that null this signal while dockerfile/yaml (imperative-payload-bearing) wire it. telemetry: no logging/analytics primitive; scroll-driven-animation constructs are already captured by events/listeners. Corpus-confirmed: data/css/{b,c}.css's probe-state/probe-telemetry/probe-cleanup keyframes are empty placeholders -- bucket-3 test (could the shell plant something real?) fails for all three; nothing exists to author.

The corpus's function construct takes no parameter list in these languages, so `args` and `avg_func_args` read low by morphology, not by an authoring gap. Shared criterion, applied per language against the live registry (gitgalaxy#2669 A.4): the construct the corpus counts as a function (the language's `func_start` rule) declares no parameters, and the `args` rule matches some *other* construct entirely, so SPEC's "each probe taking exactly one argument where the language expresses arguments" has nothing to attach to. Corpus-wide `args` totals against the 13 median: css 3, html 3, dockerfile 4, yacc 2, makefile 1, sqlite 1, cobol 1, yaml 0; `avg_func_args` is 0 or near-0 in all eight for the same reason (the hits that do exist are not inside probe bodies). Per language, with the plant-anyway option priced by running the candidate through the live compiled rules (finditer, same screening method as A.1): (css) probes are at-rules and an at-rule takes a condition, not a parameter list; the args rule matches CSS functional notation (calc|clamp|min|max|var|env|url|rgb...) inside declarations, and all 3 hits are the `url("a.css")` of the @import chain in main/a/b (c is the leaf) — i.e. args here is a byproduct of the planted `import`, the third arm of css-import-url-io-triple-overlap. `width: calc(1px + 1px)` would raise it to 13 at zero overlap cost and is DECLINED: a value expression in a declaration body is not the at-rule's parameter. (html) probes are `<script>`/`<style>` tags (themselves unreachable end-to-end, gitgalaxy#2549) and the args rule matches ATTRIBUTES (data-*, aria-*, name, value, for, ...); the 3 hits are a.html's two `data-testid` and main.html's `name="author"` ownership meta — byproducts of other plants. `<input name= value=>` also fires `api` (planted and scored); a bare `data-probe=` is clean apart from unscored structural_boundaries, and is DECLINED on the same ground: an attribute is not an argument to a callable. (yacc) probes are grammar rules and `$$`/`$n` semantic-value references are the nearest thing yacc has to a parameter surface, so this one is rejected on OVERLAP COST rather than absence: `probe_x: TOKEN { $$ = $1; }` scores args 2 AND state_mutation 1 (b.y's existing state 2 is exactly that assignment plus a counter++), so actions in the 12 productions would add 12 to a planted, scored column to move an unplanted one — the same trade cobol rejected. (yaml) probes are `run:` steps and the args rule matches a `with:` block, which in GitHub Actions binds to a `uses:` step and never to `run:` — unreachable from the corpus's function shape. Planting it costs a `uses:` line, which fires `import` AND `_dependency_capture`: fake edges in the planted main->a->b->c DAG (import = 3 corpus-wide) that the graph layer cross-checks. (makefile) probes are targets (extraction fixed by gitgalaxy#2648) and targets take no parameters; make's parameter surface is `define`/`$(call f,...)`/`$(1)`, and `define` matches the registry's `macros` rule, NOT `func_start` — converting probes to macros would delete 12 planted func_start occurrences — while `$(call ...)` additionally fires `reflection_metaprogramming`, a scored input to risk_cognitive_load. main.mk's single hit is its one `$(call probe_branch)` dispatch. (dockerfile) probes are RUN/CMD/HEALTHCHECK instructions, which take no parameters; `ARG` is a file-scoped build variable and the corpus already plants one per file (FLAG/ENVKIT/SHAPE/PLAN = 4). Nine more ARG lines are overlap-free (finditer: args only, no `globals` — unlike ENV, which is dual globals+state) and DECLINED: no instruction would consume them, so args would be measuring how many ARG lines someone typed. (sqlite) probes are CREATE INDEX statements (the #2513 tri-comparison precedent) and an index takes no parameters; args matches bind placeholders (?1, :name), `VALUES (...)` row constructors and CTE parameter lists, all of which live in DML — and every DML verb that can carry one (SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|REPLACE) is also an `io` keyword in sqlite's own rule, so each args plant costs +1 io, against a language whose io is already the batch's largest residual (#2669 B.4). main.sql's one hit is its `VALUES (1)`. (cobol) full verdict in cobol-args-clause-match-morphology (paragraphs declare no parameters; the only argument surface is the program-level PROCEDURE DIVISION USING; every per-probe alternative is also an `api` keyword); listed here so the shape is one entry and so `avg_func_args` is covered, which that entry's args-only signal did not reach. NOT in this entry, deliberately: agc_assembly. Its args rule matches register-target operands (\b(CA|CS|TS|AD|SU|...)[ \t]+(A|Q|L|Z)\b) and the AGC calling convention really does pass an argument in the accumulator, so it HAS a parameter surface; #2669 A.3 planted `CA A` at each probe entry and took args 2 -> 13, avg_func_args 0.167 -> 1.0 (the median). Resolved by authoring, not morphology — A.4's item list was written against the pre-A bias_data cache and still named it. markdown is likewise absent: its args rule is None, so the cell is n/a rather than low (markdown-lit-plane-morphology).

apex's import rule is compiled with re.IGNORECASE, which neutralises the [A-Z] guard in its second alternative (\b[a-zA-Z_]\w*\.[A-Z]\w*\b), so the alternative degrades from "lowercase receiver, capitalised member" — a type reference — to "any word.word", and every qualified method call counts as an import. Micro-repro against the live registry (engine 3ac91822): 'foo.bar', 'conn.clear' and 'Logger.info' all match; recompiling the identical pattern WITHOUT re.IGNORECASE returns nothing for all three, which isolates the flag as the entire cause. 'System.debug' and 'Database.query' are correctly excluded by the namespace lookahead. Swept every language: apex is the only rule combining re.IGNORECASE with an [A-Z] guard. Corpus effect: import 6 against a planted intent and a cross-language median of 3 — main.cls Type.forName, a.cls Type.forName, b.cls Type.forName + Logger.info + Log.error, c.cls conn.clear. The three Type.forName hits are the SPEC chain planted by gitgalaxy#2669 A.3; the other three are ordinary Apex method calls and are deliberately NOT deleted, because removing them would hide the defect rather than record it. Before A.3 apex had no chain and the count read 3 — the right number for the wrong reason, which is why the rule survived the earlier sweeps. Same family as gitgalaxy#2544 (swift's api rule counting the prose 'open'): a guard that does not guard. Filed as squid-protocol/gitgalaxy#2671 with the fix shape (scope the guard with (?-i:[A-Z]) or split the alternation, keeping IGNORECASE for the Type.forName arm since Apex is case-insensitive); collected by #2669 B.1/B.3. apex re-blesses to import 3 once it lands. RESOLVED 2026-09-02: Fixed by gitgalaxy#2671: the [A-Z] guard is restored with a scoped (?-i:[A-Z]\w*) override, so re.IGNORECASE no longer degrades the type-reference alternative to `any word.word`. apex import reblessed 6 -> 3.

fortran reads safety_bypasses 3 against a planted 2 because probe_globals plants a COMMON block, which legitimately fires BOTH rules. This is a deliberate, tested engine position, not a defect: tests/extraction/languages/test_fortran_strict.py:418 has documented it since gitgalaxy#1059 as 'an intentional double-classification, not a false collision', one of a family from the same ambiguity sweep. It is correct on the language -- a COMMON block lets distinct program units alias the same storage with no type checking, which is genuine unchecked memory sharing, unlike livecode's scope declaration or lua's bare table reference (both of which WERE over-claims and were fixed in gitgalaxy#2675). The #2650/#2659 author-header sweep touched that same test file and deliberately left COMMON alone. Filed as part of #2675 and withdrawn after review.

A probe's required idiom is legitimately also the signal being measured, so the surplus cannot be authored away without breaking the probe it belongs to. haskell safety_bypasses +2: probe_globals MUST use unsafePerformIO twice, because the globals rule requires `IORef|TVar|MVar ... unsafePerformIO`, and unsafePerformIO is genuinely the canonical Haskell safety bypass -- the only member of this family with no alternative at all. c/lua/tcl io +1 each: probe_cleanup's close idiom (`close(0)`, `io.close(conn)`, `close $conn`) is in both the cleanup and io rules, since closing a channel really is both. tcl io +3 additionally: `source` is tcl's dependency idiom AND an io keyword, the exact sibling of sqlite's `.read` (see sqlite-dot-read-dual-import-io), and it genuinely does read and evaluate a file.

control_flow_ratio = branch / (branch + structural_boundaries) (gitgalaxy detector.py:1288). The corpus pins the numerator -- branch is 3-4 in every language by design -- and never plants, gates or reports the denominator, so the whole cross-language spread is structural_boundaries, measured 0-45. It cannot be equalised by planting, because it is not a structural count: it is a per-language KEYWORD VOCABULARY tally, and the vocabularies differ in kind. ada matches six structural words (procedure|function|package|begin|end|return); python matches sixteen; solidity matches those plus every type name (uint\d*, int\d*, bytes, address, mapping); assembly matches every instruction mnemonic (mov, lea, push, pop, add, sub, ldr, str). Measured on the a.* files, where planted intent is identical: solidity 10 hits of which SIX are the type name 'uint', python 9 (def x3, return x3, from, import, assert), ada 9 (procedure x3, begin x3, end x3). Every typed declaration in solidity scores a hit its python equivalent cannot. VERDICT: the metric is not broken and no engine change is wanted -- gitgalaxy compares control_flow_ratio between files WITHIN one repository (security_auditor.py reads it that way), where the vocabulary is held constant and the ratio means what it claims. Only the cross-language comparison this corpus performs is meaningless, so the cells are explained, not fixed. Recorded in gitgalaxy#2689 (Batch D.1) bucket B, which originally proposed planting the denominator -- that recommendation was withdrawn once the rule was read. 2026-09-04 (gitgalaxy#2729 corpus wave): javascript and typescript joined, and they are the cleanest demonstration the entry has. Their api plant is `export function`, and `export` is in their structural_boundaries vocabulary -- so the denominator grew by exactly 3 per file while the numerator stayed pinned at the planted branch count, and control_flow_ratio fell out of band with not one line of control flow changed. A metric that moves when a visibility keyword is added is measuring vocabulary, which is what this entry says.

These five languages report functions_found = 16 against 13 planted. The three extra are not functions: the slicer synthesizes a __global_context__ bucket per file to hold top-level statements, and it is counted in the function population. Measured directly from the scan DB -- matlab and lua each carry exactly three __global_context__ rows in function_data alongside the 13 real probes, while python carries none. Every per-function descriptor therefore divides by 16 over a population containing three non-functions, diluting each by roughly 3/16, and cog_raw and structural_mass inherit it downstream. Same family as gitgalaxy#2547, which taught the orphan/duplicate checks to skip synthetic names via _is_synthetic_satellite_name; the per-function denominators were never given the same treatment. Filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2691 with that fix shape. Baking the current behaviour in per GATING.md rule 3 (the corpus measures what the engine does, not what it should); when #2691 lands, functions_found returns to the planted 13 and these manifests re-baseline in the same PR that flips still_reproduces. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2691, merged in gitgalaxy#2693): the engine now excludes its synthetic top-level buckets from the function population, via a `_UNCOUNTABLE_SLICE_NAMES` set narrower than the orphan check's own synthetic-name test. Verified by a fresh full-precision scan against the merged engine, not by hand: functions_found is 13 -- the planted value -- for all five languages (livecode, lua, matlab, ruby, shell), matching python. The buckets still exist and their signals are still counted at file level; only the population changed. Worth recording for whoever touches this next: the first version of the fix reused the broad orphan-check helper, which also covers "Main", and that removed go's real `func main()` from the count -- caught by tree-sitter accuracy at found_functions 897 -> 896.

These are the shape cells that survive every other explanation, and they are the interesting ones: mainstream procedural languages whose every INPUT is in band -- branch, args and LOC all green -- yet whose composite is not. The cause is the formula's deliberate non-linearity (signal_processor.py ~L800): sum_function_impacts = ((branch + 1) * sqrt(args + 1) + 0.05 * min(loc, (branch + args + 1) * 10)) * 10. A product and a clamp amplify input differences too small to flag on their own, which is precisely what makes cog_raw a cognitive-load proxy rather than a count -- a linear metric would just restate its inputs. VERDICT (gitgalaxy#2689 bucket E): affirmed as intended engine semantics, not bias, so no engine change and no re-banding. Widening the band for composites was considered and rejected: it would mask real regressions later, and the amplification is the signal. Also recorded there, so it is not re-proposed: the hypothesis that the median mixes procedural and config/DSL populations was TESTED AND REJECTED -- recomputing each metric's median over procedural languages only moves the out-of-band count by 0-1 cells (cog_raw 14 -> 14, avg_func_complexity 5 -> 5, func_internal_density 5 -> 6). SCOPE EXTENSION (2026-09-03, after gitgalaxy#2691 landed): lua's structural_mass joins this entry. It was previously attributed to the synthetic-bucket shape, and when that entry retired the cell resurfaced -- correctly, because the dilution was never the whole story for lua. Re-measured against the fixed engine: functions_found is now the planted 13 and every input is in band (branch +0%, args +0%, total_loc -5%, coding_loc -5%, state_mutation +0%), yet structural_mass sits at +41%. That is this entry's mechanism exactly. matlab's cog_raw and structural_mass resurfaced at the same moment and are NOT added here: matlab's state_mutation is +1150% (gitgalaxy#2654's return-convention shape), so its composites are attributed to that input deviation instead -- which the E.1 derivation table now does automatically, once it was corrected to include the inputs `_calc_cog_load` and `file_mass` actually read.

ada measures avg_func_args 3.0 against a corpus median of 1.0 (+200%) while planting exactly one parameter per probe function, like every other language. Cause traced to detector.py ~L6169: when a captured signature contains no comma the counter falls back to len(args_str.split()), a whitespace split written for Lisp/Scheme/Shell space-separated arguments. Ada's 'procedure Probe_Globals (Env : Integer)' captures 'Env : Integer', which splits into ['Env', ':', 'Integer'] -- one parameter counted as three. Confirmed per function in the scan DB: all 13 ada probes report args=3 where python's identical probes report 1. Ada is the ONLY language above the median here; the 0.825 cluster is the synthetic-bucket dilution (synthetic-global-context-bucket-counts-as-a-function) and the low outliers are args-no-parameter-surface-morphology. Multi-parameter ada is worse, not better, since Ada separates parameters with semicolons: 'X : Integer; Y : Integer' splits into six. Filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2692 with the fix shape; baking current behaviour in per GATING.md rule 3 until it lands. RESOLVED (gitgalaxy#2692, merged in gitgalaxy#2693): the comma-free argument fallback now splits on `;` first and treats a colon adjacent to whitespace as a type annotation, so a single typed parameter counts as one. Verified by fresh scan: ada avg_func_args is 1.0, exactly the corpus median and the planted value. The whitespace requirement is what preserves Lisp identifiers carrying a bare colon (`foo:bar`) as the separate arguments they are.

The residual shape cells after gitgalaxy#2689's other four mechanisms are accounted for, and they are all the same thing seen from two directions: identical planted intent occupies a different number of lines per language, and every one of these metrics is normalised by function body length. Measured against a corpus median avg_func_loc of 5.125: tcl 1.0 (-80%, a proc body the slicer captures as a single line) and cobol 3.19 (-38%) sit below, so their per-line densities and complexity spreads compress; haskell 0.094, jcl 0.083 and scheme 0.058 func_internal_density sit ABOVE a 0.034 median (+175%/+144%/+69%) for the mirror-image reason -- their function bodies are the shortest in the corpus (haskell 8.5 coding_loc, jcl 6.0) so the same planted signals concentrate into fewer lines. css is the degenerate case of the same rule: its 13 'functions' are selectors, which carry no branching at all, so max_func_complexity 0.25 vs 0.75 and func_complexity_gini 0.062 vs 0.188 are measuring the absence of a construct rather than a deviation in one. VERDICT: intended morphology, no engine change -- a language cannot be made to express the same logic in the same number of lines, which is the entire premise these metrics normalise against. Distinct from the ada, synthetic-bucket and composite-non-linearity entries, each of which has a mechanical cause; this one is the irreducible remainder.

detector.py L1383 is the whole definition of orphaned_logic: `elif len(func_name) > 3 and token_counts[func_name] <= 1` -- a function is an orphan when its identifier appears once in the file. token_counts is over the entire code stream INCLUDING the definition's own tokens, so the count is a property of the language's syntax, not of whether anything calls the function. There is no call graph behind this metric. Measured over the corpus (galaxyscope --db-only --debug, 46 languages, engine 4c283edf); baseline is 2.50 orphans/file (13 probe functions, 3 called from main). Five shapes, all of them here: (1) NAME REPEATED BY SYNTAX -> 0.00: ada closes with `end Probe_Globals;`, haskell writes `probeGlobals :: Int -> Int` above the equation, livecode ends the handler by name, so the token count is 2 before anything calls it. (2) SLICE NAME SYNTHETIC OR SHORT -> 0.00: yaml's 13 slices are all named `run` (3 chars, fails the len > 3 test); sqlite's are `Declarative_Block`/`CREATE_Statement`, excluded by _is_synthetic_satellite_name. (3) NO FUNCTIONS -> 0.00: html and markdown extract none, so the count has no value (D.2's undefined family, one metric further on). (4) NAME NEVER RECURS -> 3.25, i.e. every function orphaned: cobol paragraphs, m4 macros, scheme defines, make targets, abap forms, jcl steps and objective-c methods are written once and invoked by other means. (5) css 1.00: its three @keyframes slices share the name `keyframes`, which suppresses them, leaving only main.css's media/supports/container. Identical planted intent in every language, so the whole spread is measurement. Filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2727 with the fix shape (count occurrences outside the function's own [start_idx, end_idx] span, which leaves recursion correctly reading as unused); current behaviour baked into the manifests per docs/GATING.md until it lands.

raw_arch_api is the api RULE count, snapshotted before galaxyscope.py L2228's Contextual Baseline Fix converts orphans into api (#2536 added the snapshot; see the api-contextual-baseline-fix entry for the conversion itself). Measured: the rule fires in only 10 of the 44 languages that define one, so the corpus median is 0 and these ten read as the outliers -- c 7.25, python / embedded_python / fortran / lua / scala / livecode 3.25, css / makefile / html 0.25. They are not deviant; they are the only languages measuring anything. The other 36 read 0 because the probe programs contain no construct their api rule recognises: shell's rule is `^export NAME` and no probe exports, go's is `^func [A-Z]...` and every probe function is lowercase. Per file, shell/a.sh: manifest 3, rule 0, orphans converted 3, gate reads 3; go/a.go the same; python/a.py manifest 6 = rule 3 + orphans 3; c/a.c manifest 12 = rule 9 + orphans 3. verify_language.py builds its column map from RecordKeeper.SHORT_KEY_MAP, which maps api -> arch_api (the conflated column), so the manifests were recorded post-conversion and the gate cannot see an api rule that never fires. Filed as gitgalaxy#2729, which carries the two-part fix shape (gate reads raw_arch_api the way bias_report.py's RISK_INPUT_COLUMNS already does; then ~36 languages need either an exported construct planted in their own vocabulary or a wider rule -- a corpus wave of its own, deliberately not folded into F.4). Current behaviour baked in meanwhile. RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (keyword-rosetta, gitgalaxy#2729 both halves): verify_language.py now reads raw_arch_api as `api` (RAW_COLUMNS) and pins arch_api - raw_arch_api as `api_orphan_credit` (DERIVED_KEYS), so a manifest's `api` is what the rule found and nothing else. Every manifest was re-blessed mechanically first (api := raw, credit := adjusted - raw; 36 languages honestly read 0), then the corpus wave planted an explicit public surface in each language's own vocabulary on every probe function its api rule can see. The remaining 0/1 languages are ledgered by shape (api-export-list-morphology, api-non-function-surfaces, api-no-plantable-idiom).

_calc_api_exposure (signal_processor.py L1721) opens with `if api_hits == 0: return 0.0`. These five languages score a flat 0 because their api input is 0, and it is 0 for a reason that is now traced end to end: scoring reads the ADJUSTED api, which for most languages is entirely converted orphans (see api-column-is-rule-hits-only), and these languages produce no orphans to convert -- ada/haskell because their syntax repeats the function name, yaml/sqlite because their slices are short or synthetic, dockerfile because its RUN buckets are 3-char keywords (orphan-detection-is-name-recurrence, shapes 1, 2 and 5). The input column raw_arch_api sits exactly on the corpus median of 0, so no derivation edge can carry this: the input looks normal and the output is pinned. Deliberate zero-evidence semantics of the same family as #2655 -- a file with no public surface has no public surface to expose -- so the deviation is real, explained, and not a defect on either side. It resolves when gitgalaxy#2727 gives these languages orphans again.

_calc_documentation (signal_processor.py L1535-L1553) builds measured_risk = opaque_execution + api x 2.0 and returns 0.0 when it is zero: 'a file with no public surface and no load-bearing undocumented block has nothing to document, whatever it does at runtime' (#2655's zero-evidence convention, and the comment names the rosetta html/css files as the case it was written for). These four have api 0 for the reason traced in risk-api-exposure-zero-api-shortcircuit and no function whose impact exceeds 50 without a docstring, so both terms are zero. sqlite is NOT listed: it carries load-bearing undocumented slices, so its documentation risk is measured rather than pinned. Same resolution path -- gitgalaxy#2727.

The SPEC probe table does not plant `encapsulation`: it appears in 8 of 46 manifests, and only because the rule fires on constructs the probes write for other reasons. Measured per file: go 6.75 (the rule counts unexported lowercase identifiers, which every probe function is), zig 4.50, perl 3.75 (`my` scoping), agc_assembly 11.50 with nothing planted at all, css / python / embedded_python 0.25. The corpus median is 0 because the other 38 languages' idiom does not trip the rule. This is a vocabulary column in the sense F.3 gave control_flow_ratio: it counts how a language spells privacy, not how much privacy the planted program has, and no plant can equalise it without changing what the probes mean. Reported, not a defect; if a future batch wants it gated it needs a planted private-member construct per language first, which is a SPEC change. 2026-09-04 (gitgalaxy#2729 corpus wave): two more languages joined the shape, and for the sharpest possible reason -- the token that makes their api plant visible IS their encapsulation marker. rust's `pub` matches both rules (def_encapsulation 0 -> 3 per file), and haskell's `module A (probeGlobals, probeTest, probeSafety) where` header matches both (0 -> 1 per file). Neither is a second finding: one construct, two rules, recorded in both manifests.

signal_processor.py L515-L522: encapsulation_ratio = 1 - globals / (core_var_decl + globals), and 1.0 by definition when both are zero. `globals` is planted (2 in a.*); `core_var_decl` is NOT in the probe table, so the metric is a ratio of one controlled quantity to one uncontrolled one and moves with how many local declarations a language's syntax requires. Measured per file: html / jcl / markdown 1.0 in every file because they define no globals rule at all (n/a), so the numerator is structurally zero whatever the local count; cobol a.cpy var_decl 0 / globals 2 -> 0.0 and main.cbl 0 / 1 -> 0.0, mean 0.50, because COBOL declares its state in WORKING-STORAGE and has no local declarations to balance it (the same language fact the engine's LANGUAGE_STRICTNESS table records as no_implicit_globals: False); javascript a.js var_decl 7 / globals 2 -> 0.778, mean 0.9445, because its probe declares seven locals where the median language declares fewer. The whole corpus spread comes from the single file per language that plants globals. Deliberate formula reading an unplanted input -- the same disposition F.3 gave the risk formulas' unplanted inputs, kept as a ledger entry here because encapsulation_ratio is a measured column rather than a risk composite.

dockerfile is the only nonzero duplicate cell in 46 languages (1.00 mean) and it is a phantom. The slicer names its Mode-D/E buckets after the igniter keyword, so b.dockerfile extracts ['RUN','RUN','RUN','RUN','RUN'] and a.dockerfile ['RUN','RUN','HEALTHCHECK']. _is_synthetic_satellite_name (detector.py L830) recognises `<KEYWORD>_Statement` plus two literals, but not a bare keyword, so these reach the duplicate check at L1377 as ordinary functions -- same name, materially identical bodies, recorded as copy-pasted logic. The #2547 shape, in the duplicate check this time rather than the orphan one. Filed as gitgalaxy#2728 with the fix shape (read the is_synthetic_slice flag #2691 already stamps on every function, with the bucket names generated from the slicer's igniter table rather than hand-listed). Current behaviour baked in per docs/GATING.md.

The SPEC probe program is function-only: 12 probes plus an entry point, no type declarations, so 40 of 46 languages plant class_start 0 and the corpus median is 0. Any language whose file cannot BE a file without a container declaration therefore reads out of band, and each of these four is that: cobol main.cbl `PROGRAM-ID. ROSETTA-MAIN.` (a COBOL program IS the compilation unit) = 1; jcl main.jcl `//ROSETTA JOB` (the job card) = 1; css c.css `.rosetta-risk { ... }` -- the class selector carrying the planted `expression()`/`behavior()` bypass, and a CSS class is literally what the rule names = 1; yaml `jobs:` and the `chain:` mapping that follows it = 7 across four files, planted and gated. The engine reading is correct in every case -- these are the languages' structural containers -- and no plant can equalise it without making the probe program invalid in that language.

The extracted-class count of the same shape as container-construct-reads-as-class-start, one layer down: the median is 0 because the probe program declares no types. cobol/jcl/css as in that entry (1 each). dockerfile: `FROM b` opens a build stage, the language's only container, one per file = 4. kotlin a.kt: `object Region {}` / `object Home {}` = 2 -- these ARE the corpus's two planted `globals`, because Kotlin has no module-level mutable state and a singleton object is how the plant has to be written; the class count is a consequence of the globals plant, not a second deviation. Fixing it would mean planting kotlin's globals as something Kotlin does not have.

m4 args 18 vs a median of 13 (SPEC: 13 function definitions, one argument each). m4 macros have no parameter list -- `define(probe_globals, ...)` names no parameters and `$1` inside the body IS the parameter, so the rule counts one arg per USE, not per declaration: a.m4 5, b.m4 4, c.m4 3, main.m4 6 against 3/3/3/4 definitions. Every other language declares its one argument once in a signature and uses it however often it likes. The plant is correct (each macro takes exactly one argument); the count is the language's syntax, and equalising it would mean writing macros that never reference their own argument.

csharp globals 3 vs a median of 2. a.cs carries the two planted globals (`ConfigurationManager`, `AsyncLocal`); the third is in main.cs, where the planted high_risk_execution call `Environment.Exit(payload)` also matches the globals rule's `Environment.` prefix -- one token, two rules, both correct in isolation. C# has no way to spell process exit that does not go through a static ambient class, which is exactly what the globals rule looks for. Baked into the manifest (main.cs globals 1); the alternative is to plant a different danger call, which would test a less idiomatic construct.

functions_found dockerfile 17 and sqlite 30 against a median of 13 (the SPEC's 12 probes + entry). Neither language has functions, so the slicer's statement modes segment on the igniter keyword instead: dockerfile yields one bucket per RUN/CMD/HEALTHCHECK (5 in b.dockerfile alone), sqlite one per `CREATE_Statement`/`Declarative_Block` (7/9/6/8). The count is what the modes are designed to produce -- a statement-oriented language has no 13-function shape to match -- and the numbers scale with statement count, not with the planted program. Related but distinct: gitgalaxy#2728 is about those same buckets reaching the duplicate and orphan checks as if they were real identifiers, which IS a defect; the population count itself is not.

functions_found html 0 against a median of 13. The html func_start rule DOES match: three `<script` openers in a.html, one in b.html, three in c.html, two in main.html (nine in total, verified through coding_analysis). They do not survive into the recorded equations because the elements are empty -- `<script></script>` with no body -- so `splice` extracts no function and records func_start 0, which the manifest bakes. The emptiness is deliberate corpus design (gitgalaxy#2669 A.2 planted html's probe bodies as empty elements carrying only the signal tokens). Filling twelve script bodies would move html toward the median but changes what the html probe is testing; that is a SPEC decision, not a cell fix.

betweenness_score javascript and python 0.05 against a median of 0.0833335, with identical dependency_links (3) and popularity (0.75) -- so the DAG's edges are right and its SIZE is not. These are the only two language folders carrying an ecosystem manifest beside the four probe files: `package.json` and `pyproject.toml`. Betweenness is normalised by node count (network_risk_sensor.py's nx.betweenness_centrality), so a fifth scanned artifact lowers every centrality in the folder -- pagerank 0.2029 vs 0.2240 and closeness 0.1917 vs 0.2396 move with it. The manifests are deliberate (they are what exercises dependency extraction and the SBOM for those two ecosystems); the alternative is to exclude non-probe artifacts from the graph, which would change what the corpus measures about real repositories.

Haskell declares its whole public surface once, in the module header (`module A (probeGlobals, probeTest, probeSafety) where`), not per definition -- there is no per-function visibility keyword in the language. The api rule matches that header, so the corpus records api 1 per file against a per-function median of 3, and the count is a property of the idiom, not of how much surface the file exposes: the same header exports three probes. Planted 2026-09-04 under gitgalaxy#2729 (before it, every language's api read the converted orphan count and this difference was invisible). The header line also matches haskell's encapsulation rule (+1 per file), pinned in the manifest. Languages whose export idiom happens to be repeatable per function (scheme `(export x)`, tcl `namespace export x`, powershell `Export-ModuleMember -Function x`) plant 3 and are not in this shape.

These languages have no per-function visibility construct at all, so their api rule matches a FILE-level declaration and the corpus plants one per file: css `@property --probe-api-<file>` (custom-property registration; `:root` was rejected -- it also matches css's globals rule, a planted count), html `<div id=...>` (main reads 2: its `name="author"` ownership meta is also an api match), dockerfile `EXPOSE <port>` (also listeners + ipc_rpc_bridges, both ungated), yaml an `on:` trigger block, yacc `%define api.pure full`, agc_assembly one central-register `EQUALS` erasable assignment (also memory_alloc; c.agc reads 0 because spatial_correlation's leak/UAF dampener fires within 800 chars of its cleanup plants), cobol `LINKAGE SECTION.` in main. So api 1 per file against a per-function median of 3 is the idiom, not less surface. cobol's copybooks are the exception that proves it: `ENTRY 'PROBE-X'` IS per paragraph, so a/b/c plant 3 and only main reads 1. Planted 2026-09-04 under gitgalaxy#2729; before it every one of these read its converted orphan count instead of its rule.

Seven languages define an api rule and still record 0 after the gitgalaxy#2729 wave, for two distinct reasons, both measured in the real pipeline before the plant was rejected. (1) The rule cannot see the language's own way of making a function public: abap's FORM subroutines are public by default and the rule wants PUBLIC SECTION / REMOTE FUNCTION / EXPOSED / DEFINE VIEW, all of which need a CLASS (class_start must stay 0), RFC metadata or a CDS definition; matlab function files have no visibility syntax and the rule counts only classdef `methods` blocks; dart's public top-level functions are invisible to a rule that counts class/mixin/enum/extension/typedef declarations; objective-c's public method declaration in an @interface is invisible to a rule that counts FOUNDATION_EXPORT/OBJC_EXPORT/extern/@property; ada's rule matches a package SPEC (`package X is`) and the corpus ships .adb bodies, where a spec would be a separate compilation unit. dart and objective-c CAN be made to fire with a manufactured declaration (a typedef per probe, a property per probe) and both were measured doing so cleanly, but planting a declaration nobody would write to make the number move is exactly the measurement the corpus exists to avoid, so both stay 0 and the gap is the finding. (2) The only construct the rule accepts moves a PLANTED count: perl's `@EXPORT_OK = qw(...)` adds state_mutation +1 per file (measured: a 0->1, b 3->4, c 1->2), `push @EXPORT_OK` is state_mutation by definition, `use Exporter|parent|base` is an import hit and `our` a globals hit; sqlite's `CREATE [TEMP] VIEW` is a func_start hit in every spelling the rule accepts (and its SELECT body an io hit), `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` a class_start hit. A corpus that moves a planted count to light up a signal is measuring itself. Both halves are the same finding as the one gitgalaxy#2729 was filed for -- the api rules disagree about what a public surface is -- and the rule-too-narrow half is filed upstream as gitgalaxy#2730, which asks for a stated contract for the api rule rather than seven separate regex fixes. Resolves per language as #2730 lands, paired with the plant that the widened rule can see (AGENTS.md rule 8).

In these four the api plant NAMES the probe functions -- `global probe_x` (NASM), `Export-ModuleMember -Function probe_x`, `module_function :probe_x`, `namespace export probe_x` -- and that second occurrence of the name makes the function stop reading as an orphan: detector.py ~L1383 defines an orphan as `token_counts[func_name] <= 1` over the whole code stream, with no call graph (gitgalaxy#2727). orphaned_logic therefore reads 0, the Contextual Baseline Fix has nothing to convert, and api_orphan_credit drops 3 -> 0 in a/b/c while `api` goes 0 -> 3. The import chain still resolves (import counts unchanged), so the credit's loss is not evidence of a DAG regression -- but the credit is the gate's only assertion that the chain resolved (GATING.md 'What `api` asserts'), so these four lose that assertion and rely on the other 40 for it. Name-free alternatives exist for some (`Export-ModuleMember -Function *`, a bare `module_function`, tcl `package provide`) and were rejected: they export the entry function too, or drop the count to 1, which is worse measurement to protect a side assertion. makefile `.PHONY: probe_x` and m4 `m4_provide([probe_x])` were rejected for this exact reason during the wave -- both zeroed the credit, and `export VAR` / `AC_SUBST` plant the same api count without naming a function, so those two languages keep their credit. Resolves when gitgalaxy#2727 makes the orphan census count occurrences outside the function's own span: a mention in an export statement is outside the span, so it will still clear the flag -- the honest fix is a real call graph, which #2727 records as the open design question. SIGNAL SCOPE: the same fact is visible in the bias report as `raw_state_slop_orphans` (3.25 -> 0 per file in these four against a corpus median of 2.50), which is the column the report measures; `api_orphan_credit` is the manifest key for it. Both are named so the gate and the report join on the same finding.

jcl and markdown are the only corpus languages whose registry entry defines NO api rule, so the rule count is structurally 0 while the post-gitgalaxy#2729 median is 3. Neither has a public-surface concept to plant: a JCL job exposes nothing to a caller (its `api` was only ever the orphan conversion -- see batch5-tier2-morphology-shapes), and a markdown document declares no callable surface at all (markdown-lit-plane-morphology). This cell was invisible before #2729 because the report scored the ADJUSTED column, whose corpus median was 0. Marking it n/a instead of ledgering it would need an n/a mechanism in the report's measures group, which does not exist today, and would remove the audited rows (`markdown/api`, `jcl/api`) that na_check.py's derived-cell review depends on.

`_calc_api_exposure` and `_calc_documentation` read the ADJUSTED api (`arch_api` = rule hits + converted orphans); the report measures the RAW rule count, so no derivation edge can attribute these cells -- the measured input sits on the median while the output does not. The same three identifiers are counted once as declarations and once as converted orphans, because the Contextual Baseline Fix never asks whether the api rule already counted them. Both directions of this entry's cells follow: the 18 risk_api_exposure languages declare visibility AND convert orphans, so their scored api is doubled and their exposure sits off the median; livecode, ruby and tcl declare visibility but have no orphans left to convert (livecode's syntax repeats the handler name, ruby's and tcl's export statements name the function -- api-export-names-suppress-orphan-credit), so their scored api is HALF the planted group's and risk_documentation sits low. Invisible before the #2729 wave: no corpus language had both halves at once, and the report's api median was 0. Resolves when #2731 credits only the orphans the rule did not already count.

Markdown is prose: no execution model (concurrency, sync_locks), no visibility construct (encapsulation), no const/freeze concept (immutability_locks), no metaprogramming facility (reflection_metaprogramming). Fenced code blocks are literate content owned by the #691 lit_* comment-stream rules, not commented-out code, so dead_code has nothing distinct to measure. spec_exposure's generic bracket-tag pattern ([SPEC-n]/[spec .../[audit ...]) collides with markdown link syntax -- any link whose text begins spec/audit would FP -- so that absence is deliberate, not an oversight. Completes the prose-morphology family alongside the existing markdown structure/signal entries.

No async-execution construct exists in these languages, per-language: css -- declarative styling; animations/transitions are declarative timelines the renderer schedules, nothing code-visible is asynchronous execution. jcl -- steps within a job execute strictly sequentially by definition; parallelism lives in JES scheduling/config outside the language's own syntax. m4 -- strictly sequential single-threaded text expansion. solidity -- the EVM executes transactions atomically and single-threaded; no threads/async/futures (the reentrancy surface is already owned by sync_locks nonReentrant and reflection_metaprogramming delegatecall/call). yacc -- a grammar has no execution model of its own; considered %pure-parser / %define api.pure (declares the generated parser's reentrancy, i.e. the absence of shared state, rather than serializing access to it) and rejected.

No lock/serialization construct exists, per-language: css and html -- markup and styling have no shared mutable state to serialize (html's closest stability idioms readonly/disabled/inert are already owned by its immutability_locks rule). m4 -- sequential expansion, no shared state. yacc -- grammar layer, same reasoning as its concurrency absence. yaml -- the one mutex-shaped construct in yaml.py's target ecosystem, GitHub Actions concurrency: groups (with cancel-in-progress), is already owned by the concurrency rule (^concurrency:); a sync_locks rule would re-count the same token -- the cobol-api overlap-cost rejection precedent.

No visibility/privacy construct: jcl -- PROCs and symbolic parameters are parameterization, not privacy; nothing in JCL syntax hides one statement from another. yaml -- plain data; GH Actions secrets.* is access to a secret store and is already owned by the globals rule (${{ secrets. }}), not an encapsulation idiom.

immutability_locks: JCL has no const concept. Considered LABEL=(,,,IN) read-only open and PROTECT=YES -- dataset-protection attributes, rare in real decks, not language-level immutability; rejected. reflection_metaprogramming: symbolic substitution (SET &X= / &X. use-sites) is parameterization -- SET is already owned by state_mutation, and the analogous shell $VAR expansion is likewise not counted as reflection in shell.py. Strongest candidate INCLUDE MEMBER=&NAME (dynamic include) rejected: parameterized inclusion, owned by import.

The engine's own registry records the rationale in-code: m4.py annotates the None rule with 'M4 macros are mutable by design'. define/undefine freely rebind any macro at any time -- mutability is the language's core mechanism; no freeze/const construct exists to measure.

Missing rules, not morphology. dead_code (jcl) and spec_exposure (jcl, yaml) are comment-stream rules (detector.comment_analysis) absent where the stream exists: for jcl this is the #2610 leftover shape -- the comment stream was structurally empty until _strip_jcl_comments, and #2610 added debt/ownership rules but never revisited these two; for yaml the absence is arbitrary (# comments always reached comment_analysis, and flow-sequence brackets cannot FP because spec_exposure never sees the code stream; yaml is one of only three rosetta languages without the otherwise-generic tag rule). Evidence: 14 pool .jcl/.prc files carry //*-commented-out statements including whole JOB cards. Filed with fix shapes and the GATING paired-plant note (the corpus currently plants neither idiom). Scope note: yaml/dead_code is NOT covered by this entry -- yaml defines that rule; classify_na only reads (lang, signal) pairs that are actually absent. Retires (still_reproduces -> false) when the rules land.

Real serialization morphology with a rule-design conflict: DISP=OLD/MOD request an exclusive system ENQ on a dataset (DISP=SHR shared) -- z/OS's native lock idiom, and the engine already maps sync_locks onto a language's own idiom (solidity nonReentrant). But DISP= is already a keyword in jcl's io rule, and #2610 explicitly rejected a cleanup rule on DISP=(...,DELETE/CATLG) for exactly that double-count; counterweight: the engine tolerates semantic overlaps where meanings differ (COND=((4,LT),EVEN) counts safety AND safety_bypasses; haskell finally counts cleanup+safety). Filed as a design question with a narrowed OLD/MOD-only shape. Either outcome -- rule added with a paired DISP=OLD plant, or declined per the cleanup precedent -- ends the unreviewed state; this entry flips to record the decision.
